title: A precise opening offer
hook: Would $4,988 and $5,000 invite the same counteroffer?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Identify opening-price precision as distinct from the opening-price level.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Identify opening-price precision as distinct from the opening-price level.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy quote is rounded to the nearest €1,000 and shown as €5,000. Which range could round to that quote? Toy inputs A=[5000, 1000]; B=[4988, 1].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.
compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Under the stated rounding convention, precision changes the implied interval around the quote. A precise first offer may convey different information, but this arithmetic does not predict a negotiator’s response.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Quoted €=4988, Rounding €=1. What is Mid €? Answer: 4988.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Quoted €=4988, Rounding €=1. What is Mid €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 4988. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Precise opening prices like $4,988 draw smaller counteroffers than round ones like $5,000 (Janiszewski & Uy, 2008; Mason et al., 2013).
sourceProvenance.pointer: 500-behavioral-economics-findings.md entry 29: Janiszewski & Uy, 2008; Mason et al., 2013
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Identify opening-price precision as distinct from the opening-price level.
